        From 7055a29471eebf4b62687944694222635ed44b09 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Maor Gottlieb <maorg@mellanox.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Aug 2016 14:16:30 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] IB/mlx5: Fix steering resource leak

Fix multicast flow rule leak on adding unicast rule failure.

Fixes: 038d2ef87572 ('IB/mlx5: Add flow steering support')
Signed-off-by: Maor Gottlieb <maorg@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Doug Ledford <dledford@redhat.com>
---
 drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c
index 840fbd0c9dca..87988fbc87b4 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c
@@ -1861,6 +1861,7 @@ static struct mlx5_ib_flow_handler *create_leftovers_rule(struct mlx5_ib_dev *de
 						 &leftovers_specs[LEFTOVERS_UC].flow_attr,
 						 dst);
 		if (IS_ERR(handler_ucast)) {
+			mlx5_del_flow_rule(handler->rule);
 			kfree(handler);
 			handler = handler_ucast;
 		} else {
--

        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The root cause of the bug was a resource leak that occurred when adding a unicast flow rule failed. Specifically, when the function `create_leftovers_rule` attempted to create a unicast flow rule and it returned an error (indicated by `IS_ERR(handler_ucast)`), the existing multicast flow rule was not properly deleted, leading to a leak of resources associated with that rule. The patch addresses this by ensuring that the multicast flow rule is deleted using `mlx5_del_flow_rule(handler->rule)` before freeing the handler, thus preventing the resource leak.

Root cause:
The root cause of the bug was a resource leak that occurred when adding a unicast flow rule failed. Specifically, when the function `create_leftovers_rule` attempted to create a unicast flow rule and it returned an error (indicated by `IS_ERR(handler_ucast)`), the existing multicast flow rule was not properly deleted, leading to a leak of resources associated with that rule. The patch addresses this by ensuring that the multicast flow rule is deleted using `mlx5_del_flow_rule(handler->rule)` before freeing the handler, thus preventing the resource leak.
